arithmetic.question: does a memory that is allowed not to look buy the perception it skips, and at what price does the trade-off first become visible
arithmetic.model_change: World::read_period: a `Memory` organism reads its two neighbours only when step % read_period == 0 and acts on `direction()` in between; `Sighted` is not gated. At read_period = 1 nothing changes -- three recorded hashes were checked against a worktree binary built from HEAD (random de3950f7ae833acf, sighted 46691241b93abff9, memory 66cdac546d4289a5)
arithmetic.grid: P_need in {1,2} x field in {uniform, peaks-6} x read_budget in {1,3} x read_cost in {0.0,0.02,0.05} x read_period in [1, 2, 4, 8] x arms ['sighted', 'intact', 'stay', 'random'], start cell 3, seed 3, horizon 20000 steps

read_bill_per_step.why_it_decides: the reserve is 5.0 and upkeep is `m`, so at rb=3 and a price of 0.05 the reads alone drain 0.10 per step; FINDING-156 measured sighted and intact at 51 steps there. Dividing the looks by p divides that drain by p, which is the only way a memory can buy time -- unless the stale address is worse than the fresh comparison, which is the failure mode this can run into

arithmetic.stale_memory_term: a memory stores a LEVEL and an ADDRESS. On `uniform` every cell regrows toward the same ceiling M, so a remembered address is still a decent cell when the organism arrives. On `peaks-6` the address can be a poor cell whose ceiling is 0.2, and the memory cannot tell until it reads again. Staleness must therefore cost more on `peaks-6`, and the gain over period 1 must be smaller
arithmetic.why_rb1_is_the_control: with read_budget = 1 the own cell consumes the whole budget, so no neighbour is read at any period and no read cost is paid: the period can change neither lifetime nor hash. That is the `specific` control's silent half
arithmetic.mde_note: sigma = 1000 steps between seeds, target effect 250 steps -> 252 arms per cell; the grid has 4 periods per cell, so differences below 250 steps are `void`, not `failed`. The claims rest on horizon-sized contrasts (a death before 20000 against survival)

prediction.a_no_gain_at_zero_price: read_cost = 0: for every point/field/rb, intact at period > 1 must NOT outlive intact at period = 1. The look is free, so skipping it can only throw information away. CAN FAIL if the stale address happens to beat the fresh comparison through the tie-break drift: the memory walks a remembered cell while `sighted` compares and stays on a tie
prediction.b_gain_at_a_positive_price: read_cost = 0.05, uniform, P_need = 2, rb = 3: intact at period 4 must outlive intact at period 1 by more than mde (250 steps). The bill falls from 0.10 to 0.025 per step and 156's death at 51 steps is the price of reading, so the reserve should last about four times longer. CAN FAIL: the stale memory walks to a cell that has already been eaten and the organism starves looking for it
prediction.c_optimum_period_grows_with_price: argmax over period of intact lifetime is 1 at read_cost = 0 and non-decreasing in price; at 0.05 it is > 1 on uniform P_need = 2, rb = 3. That is the transition surface the two reviews said exists without a constant. CAN FAIL: if staleness costs more than the reads it saves the surface is flat or tilts back to 1
prediction.d_peaks_gain_smaller_than_uniform: the best gain over period (max_p lifetime(p) - lifetime(1)) on peaks-6 is smaller than on uniform at the same point/rb/cost, because a remembered address on an uneven field can be a poor cell whose ceiling is 0.2, while a uniform address keeps regrowing toward M. CAN FAIL: if the peaked field is so harsh that all arms die in a few steps, both gains are zero and the comparison is not informative -- that is not evidence for the prediction

verdict.reason: EXPLAINED: The trade-off appears in the direction the arithmetic predicted, but not at the size this instrument can certify. (a) At read_cost=0 the control is silent: best gain 0 steps, so rarer reading is never better when reading is free -- knowledge ages and nothing is saved. (b) At a positive price it is better: the best positive-price gain is only 37 steps, below the 250-step mde; the optimum period on uniform P_need=2, rb=3 moves [1, 2, 4] as the price goes 0.00 -> 0.02 -> 0.05, so (c) holds in direction. (d) the gain on `peaks-6` is not uniformly smaller than on `uniform`; and on the informative rows the peaked field is not just less rewarding but catastrophic: the same skip costs up to 19994 steps (20000 -> 6). The mechanism is not the guessed one -- a Memory advances at most one cell per sampling interval, so crossing the 3-cell poor basin costs p*3 steps while the reserve covers only 5.52 poor steps. The gain itself is 33-37 steps, below the 250-step mde, and by the pre-registered rule a sub-mde difference is `void`, not `passed`: one seed cannot separate it from the between-seed spread. What is horizon-sized is the OTHER side of the trade-off -- the cost of not reading on an uneven field. `void`: the mechanism is measured, its size is not certified.

limitations: one seed and one start cell. The start (cell 3) is poor and equidistant from the peaks of `peaks-6`, so the arms that never move and the arms that look start from the same place; with the probe's default start of 0 the stationary arms start on a peak and the comparison would be biased toward them.

a memory stores an ADDRESS and a LEVEL seen earlier; it has no model of regrowth. `direction()` can therefore walk to a cell whose level it remembers but which has been eaten since. This is exactly the staleness term the experiment prices, not a defect to fix before measuring it.
one organism, no competition, no sharing; the probe wraps movement on a ring while `Life` does not -- the same structural limits as FINDING-155 and FINDING-156.
`income = upkeep` by construction. At P_need=2 a cell held by one organism settles below the upkeep, so only movement pays: the two points are two media, not two prices of one medium.

the probe's own hash does not mix read_period, so control arms that never read (stay, random) and `sighted` share one hash across the period axis by construction. That is declared in `expected_coincident` and is the `specific` control's evidence, not a collision of the experimental arms.
